title: Skip Priority lines in the Queue a request commit subject
summary: `Athena::queue` in reading.rs builds "Queue a request: <first line>" from the request's raw first line, so a request starting "Priority: urgent" is titled by its priority. The fix uses the existing `plan::title_line` helper, which skips Priority and blank lines, and adds a test and a CHANGELOG entry. The audience is anyone reading the records log.

defaults_applied.how: New test plus cargo test and clippy criteria
One focused change that reuses the existing title_line helper
Checks that the Dropped path also uses the shared helper, not only the Queue path
The test asserts the actual commit subject
Criteria are commands the verifier can run
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs `queue` (about lines 895-932) takes `request.text.lines().next()` truncated to 60 chars for the subject. crates/athena-core/src/plan.rs already has `pub fn title_line` (line 114), which skips Priority: lines and blanks and has its own tests. crates/athena-core/src/store.rs `title()` already uses it. crates/athena-core/src/manage.rs close builds its subjects from `job.title()`, which is `title_line`-based when there is no reading. No records or data file is added, so no record allow-list is affected.

The 'Dropped:' subject is probably already correct, because it comes from `job.title()` in store.rs, which uses `title_line`. The producer should confirm this with a Grep and change it only if some path still takes the raw first line. Nothing under crates/athena-gate needs to change.
The 60-character truncation stays. `title_line` returns the first line when every line is a Priority or blank line, and that fallback is kept.

The test goes in the existing tests module of reading.rs. It calls `queue` through the existing test helpers, with a request like 'Priority: urgent\n\nFix the widget', and reads the commit subject back with git log.
No governance files change. CHANGELOG.md is the only non-code deliverable.

acceptance_criteria.text: In crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs, the `queue` subject uses `crate::plan::title_line(&request.text)` (then the 60-char cap) instead of `lines().next()`; check the diff.

A new test in reading.rs queues a request whose first line is 'Priority: urgent' followed by a real request line. It asserts the commit subject is 'Queue a request: <real line>' and does not contain 'Priority'. Check with `cargo test -p athena-core` and the test name in the diff.
The diff shows no raw first-line subject left for a Dropped commit. The Dropped subject path (manage.rs via `job.title()`) is either shown to use `title_line` or changed to use it.
CHANGELOG.md has a new entry under the unreleased section saying that queued and dropped request commit subjects skip leading Priority lines.
`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets`, and `cargo test` all pass, and the existing `title_line` tests in plan.rs still pass unchanged.
The diff touches only reading.rs, CHANGELOG.md, and plan.rs or manage.rs if needed; no other behavior changes.

out_of_scope: Changing how Priority is parsed or how priority affects plan ordering
Changing titles taken from a reading
Changes to athena.toml, defaults.toml or workflows
departures: The change is small: a helper already exists, so cost and time are below the reference.
